List the pathways whose history most changes the prediction

Source: R/pathways.R
divergent_pathways.Rd

divergent_pathways() returns the pathways whose next-state distribution departs most from that of their parent, the same pathway without its oldest state, measured by the Kullback-Leibler divergence in bits. These are the places where remembering one more state of history changes what is expected next, and therefore where the process depends on more than its most recent state. With flips_only = TRUE, only pathways whose most likely next state differs from the parent's are returned.

Divergence is computed from smoothed probabilities and can be large for rare pathways; set min_count to exclude them, and use bootstrap_pathways() to check whether a divergence is stable under resampling. The root, which has no parent, is never returned.

Usage

divergent_pathways(tree, top = 10L, min_count = 1L, flips_only = FALSE)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

top

Number of pathways to return. Default 10.

min_count

Keep pathways that occurred at least this many times. Default 1.

flips_only

Return only pathways whose most likely next state differs from the parent's. Default FALSE.

Value

A data.frame with the columns of tree_pathways(), one row per pathway, sorted by divergence in decreasing order, at most top rows.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree.

See also

tree_pathways(), tree_dependence(), plot_divergence(), bootstrap_pathways().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
divergent_pathways(tree, top = 5, min_count = 20)
#>                               pathway depth count likely_next next_probability
#> 1                          Disengaged     1   325  Disengaged        0.4830769
#> 2                              Active     1   658      Active        0.6975684
#> 3                Active -> Disengaged     2    23      Active        0.3913043
#> 4         Average -> Active -> Active     3    70      Active        0.5285714
#> 5 Disengaged -> Disengaged -> Average     3    31     Average        0.7085484
#>   divergence changes_prediction
#> 1  0.4030656               TRUE
#> 2  0.3494872               TRUE
#> 3  0.3478095               TRUE
#> 4  0.2330062              FALSE
#> 5  0.1984047              FALSE
divergent_pathways(tree, flips_only = TRUE)
#>                               pathway depth count likely_next next_probability
#> 3                          Disengaged     1   325  Disengaged        0.4830769
#> 4     Disengaged -> Average -> Active     3    12     Average        0.8318333

#> 6                Active -> Disengaged     2    23      Active        0.3913043
#> 7     Active -> Average -> Disengaged     3    17      Active        0.4117647
#> 10    Active -> Disengaged -> Average     3     7  Disengaged        0.5707143
#> 18 Disengaged -> Disengaged -> Active     3     9     Average        0.5555556
#> 23              Average -> Disengaged     2   134     Average        0.5000000
#> 24   Average -> Disengaged -> Average     3    64  Disengaged        0.4843750
#> 30       Average -> Active -> Average     3    64      Active        0.4531250
#>    divergence changes_prediction
#> 3  0.40306556               TRUE
#> 4  0.39333418               TRUE
#> 5  0.34948716               TRUE
#> 6  0.34780951               TRUE
#> 7  0.31329586               TRUE
#> 10 0.20137567               TRUE
#> 18 0.10602662               TRUE
